title: When do the nearest hundred and nearest thousand agree?
description: Vijay rounds a distance to the nearest hundred and Suma to the nearest thousand. The video lists both answers for each given number and circles the ones that match.
teaching_notes: One idea: find both rounded answers for a number and compare them. Watch for a child who says a number near a thousand always gives the same answer both ways.

source: Let Us Think 1, Vijay and Suma
video_script.why: The child can find the nearest hundred and nearest thousand separately, but has not compared the two for one number.
video_script.substitution: Find the nearest hundred and nearest thousand for each number and keep the numbers where the two answers match.
video_script.anchor: Vijay and Suma reading the same distance number on a signboard
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says seven thousand one hundred and twenty six is close to seven thousand, so both answers are seven thousand. The nearest hundred is seven thousand one hundred.

final_answer.spoken: seven thousand and thirty, and six thousand nine hundred and ninety nine

maths_rules: 7,126: nearest hundred 7,100 (26 jumps), nearest thousand 7,000 (126 jumps); different
check: a number less than 50 away from a whole thousand gives the same answer both ways
video_script.design: Exercise. Hint: find both answers for each number and compare. A sample number, 7,210, shows two different answers before the child tries.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Vijay and Suma read the same distance number on a signboard.
<bookmark mark='vs'/>Vijay rounds it to the nearest hundred, and Suma rounds it to the nearest thousand.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Both get the same answer. Which of the four numbers in your book could it be?

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: one sample number 7,210 gets two answers side by side: nearest hundred 7,200 and nearest thousand 7,000, marked as different
narration: <bookmark mark='ex'/>Take any number, like seven thousand two hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Its nearest hundred is seven thousand two hundred, but its nearest thousand is seven thousand.
<bookmark mark='hint'/>Do the same for each number in your book, and compare. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 7,126 is close to 7,000 so both are 7,000; Vijay's nearest hundred 7,100 is shown beside it; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Seven thousand one hundred and twenty six is close to seven thousand, so both are seven thousand.
<bookmark mark='vijay'/>Vijay rounds to the nearest hundred, so he stops at seven thousand one hundred.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is not seven thousand, so Vijay and Suma do not agree.

marks.b: the row 7,835: 7,800 and 8,000 appears marked differ

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>List both answers for each number, because the two answers must match.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Seven thousand one hundred and twenty six gives seven thousand one hundred, and seven thousand. They differ.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Seven thousand eight hundred and thirty five gives seven thousand eight hundred, and eight thousand. They differ.

beats.on_screen: the table adds 7,030 gives 7,000 and 7,000, match; 6,999 gives 7,000 and 7,000, match; the numbers 7,030 and 6,999 are circled

marks.c: the row 7,030: 7,000 and 7,000 appears marked match
marks.d2: the row 6,999: 7,000 and 7,000 appears marked match

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Seven thousand and thirty gives seven thousand, and seven thousand. They match.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Six thousand nine hundred and ninety nine is one jump below seven thousand.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Both answers are seven thousand, so they match.
<bookmark mark='end'/>Vijay and Suma could have used seven thousand and thirty, or six thousand nine hundred and ninety nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, see how far the number is from a whole thousand.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>If it is less than fifty away, both answers match.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Seven thousand and thirty is thirty away, so it passes.
